Reference Architecture: 1. The Advanced Single-Engine Commuter (e.g., Cirrus SR22 Hybrid Concept)
Description: A centralized series-hybrid architecture. The ICE occupies the nose, while a single electric motor is mounted in the tail. It utilizes futuristic solid-state batteries and Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) to save weight. Designed for Part 23 Normal category, it relies on a Simplex FCC but compensates with a ballistic parachute (CAPS).
Why Chosen as Reference: Serves as the lower-bound complexity baseline. It validates the minimal redundancy paths (Simplex FCC, minimal k=2 LRU partitioning constraint) and tests the mutually exclusive spatial constraints of the Series topology (Nose is blocked by the generator, forcing the single motor to the Tail station).

Reference Architecture: 2. The Conventional Part 23 Twin Retrofit (e.g., Diamond DA62 Hybrid / Ampaire EEL)
Description: A parallel-hybrid twin-engine configuration. The ICE and electric motors mechanically drive two wing-root propellers simultaneously. Employs mature Li-Ion NMC batteries and dual-redundant, federated avionics typical of present-day commercial commuter platforms without whole-airframe parachutes.
Why Chosen as Reference: Represents the industry-standard evolutionary step (TRL 8-9). It anchors the design space in present-day feasibility. Utilizing dual-redundancy forces the k=3 LRU partitioning constraint, while the parallel topology accurately limits the Nose position, demonstrating standard architectural constraint propagation.

Reference Architecture: 3. The Distributed Electric e-STOL (e.g., NASA X-57 Maxwell Paradigm)
Description: A high-redundancy, turboelectric quad-motor distributed propulsion system. Utilizes thermally stable LFP batteries and triple-redundant FCCs for fly-by-wire reliability. Uses IMA to efficiently manage the complex distributed thrust logic safely across 4 wing-mounted motors.
Why Chosen as Reference: Pushes the upper bounds of the architectural space for performance and fault tolerance. It heavily activates the most restrictive ADG constraints: Turboelectric blocks both the Nose and Tail from D4, while the Triple-redundant FCCs strictly enforce fault-isolation rules in D7, requiring exactly k=3 LRU packages.
